The U.S. government yesterday announced updates to its list of prohibited foreign-made products, adding "advanced robotic devices" to the roster. An FCC spokesperson confirmed today that the ban also applies to robot vacuums.

The robot vacuum ban affects Roomba, Roborock, and other major brands—but you can keep using the one you already have

When the Trump administration announced yesterday that "advanced robotic devices" would be banned from entering the U.S., headlines focused on humanoid robots. But espionage doesn't require legs—and the FCC's robot ban doesn't discriminate either. Katie Gorscak, the FCC's director of media relations, confirmed to The Verge that robot vacuums will fall under the ban. The authorities are not coming to confiscate your existing Roomba—companies can continue importing and selling already-approved products. However, the government claims that future foreign-made robots pose a national security risk, and even robot vacuum companies are suddenly being asked to commit to manufacturing in the U.S.

The FCC considers advanced robotic devices a national security risk, and that reasoning applies to products generally considered harmless as well—robot vacuums, robotic lawnmowers, and the like.

Unless a device is explicitly approved, or manufactured on U.S. soil, it will not be allowed to be sold in the country.

This ban has particularly far-reaching implications for robot vacuums, as top brands like Roomba, Roborock, and Ecovacs are all owned by Chinese companies.

If you currently own any of these products, you can continue using them today without any impact. The FCC is not going to send anyone to confiscate your robot vacuum.

Depending on how the ban is implemented, however, the robot vacuum market could see dramatic shifts in the short term. If this all sounds familiar, it's because the ban mirrors the one imposed on wireless routers just a few months ago.

Will you continue using your existing robot vacuum? Why or why not? Share your thoughts in the comments.
